contract: Read one preloaded finite DVB DTS-HD stream with two or four extension substreams and no core. TS 102 114 V1.6.1 7.5.2 permits up to four indexed extension substreams; F.4.3 requires exactly one complete access unit per aligned finite PES when multiple substreams are present.

Compare the complete ordered packet fold with the parser-enabled FFmpeg demuxer without stream discovery. The pinned demuxer exposes this DVB extension descriptor as bin_data and preserves the PES access-unit boundary, unset duration, clear key flag and original PES position. The candidate verifies substream order, DWORD alignment, extents and every header CRC before publishing the original complete unit.

The comparison uses the existing demux-clock and packet-field projections. Public packets keep original source PTS/DTS, exact primary-extension duration and PES payload ranges. Reader tests verify these source fields separately. The explicit DTS parser splits these multi-extension units into individual substreams, so this feature compares the demuxer packets and keeps the grouped single-extension source comparison separate.

Inputs are independently authored framing controls with opaque asset bodies. They cover TS188 and M2TS192, short and long headers, zero alignment padding, inherited timing, PTS-only, PTS/DTS and untimed PES. Generate them with cargo xtask fixture transport-dts-hd-grouped or cargo xtask fixtures; no generated media is committed.
